Owens was initially charged with 14 felonies but reached a deal in August, pleading guilty to two counts of fraudulent schemes and artifices, one count of perjury and one count of taking the identity of another.
Laura Owens was sentenced to 30 days in jail and seven years of probation for fabricating medical records and faking pregnancies to target men.
The judge imposed 30 days of flat time plus 12 months of deferred jail starting Oct. 22, 2027, and warned Owens she faces up to 12.5 years in prison if she violates probation.
Judge Jeffrey Rueter delivered the sentence in the high-profile Arizona case in Maricopa County Superior Court in Phoenix.
The judge opted against prison time, citing Owens' lack of criminal history, her mental health issues, and her remorse as mitigating factors.
